D.t: Jeff Merkley leads by 30.1 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 617,570 votes; a one point swing is about 10,276 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +21.5 and D +38.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Multnomah, a projected net 289,922 votes; Washington, a projected net 137,582 votes; Lane, a projected net 80,902 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Yamhill, D +7.3, 2.5% of the vote; Polk, D +10.6, 2.1% of the vote; Coos, R +5.5, 1.6% of the vote; Columbia, R +2.1, 1.4% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jeff Merkley runs furthest behind in Klamath, Linn, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 81% of voters, 59 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.04 points; Voters without a degree, 55% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.77 points; Men, 46% of voters, 58 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.31 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jeff Merkley: Immigration voters 25 to 72, Small counties 46 to 50, Midsize counties 50 to 46. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
